messages:
Jess (support): Heads up — starting ~09:12 UTC we have multiple tickets from AP-SOUTHEAST-2 (apse2) customers: generation requests returning 502/504 and long timeouts. Customers report both streaming and non-streaming endpoints failing.
Tom (sre-oncall): I'm seeing a sharp spike in 5xx from the edge gateway in apse2-b, tail latency up, error budget alerts firing. Routers show higher retransmits.
Jess (support): Example curl from a customer:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' 
  -d '{"model":"x-large-2025","prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{ "error": { "message": "gateway timeout", "request_id": "req_apse2_9f7a" } }
```
Ravi (eng-runtime): Can you paste the request IDs and any edge logs? I want to check whether requests reached the runtime or failed at the gateway.
Jess (support): IDs: req_apse2_9f7a, req_apse2_9fb2, req_apse2_9ff1. Support console shows gateway TTL expired, upstream connect timed out.
Tom (sre-oncall): Dashboard snippet: edge-gateway 5xx rate jumped at 09:12:14 -> 09:40, peaking at 18% error rate for apse2-b. Pod logs show connection reset to upstream runtime. No runtime OOMs.
Sam (networking): We're seeing interconnect packet loss and intermittent BGP session flaps on our primary transit to the apse2 region peer. Provider announced withdraws toward our AS for ~3.5m windows. Provider ticket 84231 opened.
CarrierBot: Provider event: "transit-metro-01 — BGP neighbor 203.0.113.17 session reset; withdraws observed; high loss toward 10.4.0.0/21" (ticket 84231).
Sam (networking): Here's a quick traceroute collected from an edge gateway (apse2-b) at 09:15:
```
traceroute to 10.4.12.45 (10.4.12.45), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  1.9 ms  2.0 ms  1.8 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.17  30.2 ms  28.9 ms  31.1 ms
 5  198.51.100.18  120 ms  220 ms  310 ms

# intermittent * and extreme jitter, consistent with packet loss on provider hop
```
Lina (support-ops): Support queue: 14 distinct customers affected, 6 escalations to enterprise sales already. Customers asking for RTO and whether we can failover to other region.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Two mitigation paths: 1) Route selector fallback at the API gateway to prefer apse2-c or apse1 (if model/latency acceptable). 2) Temporarily increase upstream connect timeout and enable additional retries (careful — could increase duplicate billing usage).
Tom (sre-oncall): I'm going to flip a targeted routing policy for canary traffic (5% -> apse2-c) and enable automatic fallback for requests that hit the gateway connect timeout. DeployBot: rolling that change to the gateway.
DeployBot: started rollout 09:28 UTC (config: gateway.fallback.apse2 5%->apse2-c, connect_timeout=10s, retries=2)
Jess (support): Notifying affected customers now with ETA 30m and asking them to retry.
Sam (networking): Provider is seeing partial convergence issues on their MPLS link; their NOC confirmed carrier PE out-of-memory thrash during route churn (they're patching). They are advertising alternate path now.
CarrierBot: Provider update — partial mitigation applied at 09:33 UTC, withdrawal rate reduced; monitoring for >= 30m.
Tom (sre-oncall): Post-mitigation metrics: error rate dropped from 18% -> 3% by 09:36. Latency stabilized but some tail spikes persist until 09:42.
Jess (support): Customers reporting improved behavior, some full restores. Still seeing retries/duplicate errors for a few streams. Logged affected request IDs for billing reconciliations.
Ravi (eng-runtime): We should collect end-to-end traces for all impacted request IDs and tag them for the postmortem. Also add a temporary rule to avoid double-charging on automatic retries for the affected window (09:12-09:40 UTC).
Lina (support-ops): Creating support incident bundle (INC-2026-153) with all customers and initial L2 notes. Assigning to billing team to review retry-charge exceptions.
Sam (networking): Action items assigned to provider: verify BGP config and PE memory patch results by EOD, share root cause (ticket 84231). We've requested packet captures for 09:10-09:40 window.
Tom (sre-oncall): Short-term: keep fallback routing enabled for 1h, then ramp down after monitoring horizon. Long-term: add multi-carrier peering in apse2 to avoid single transit dependency.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Also lower default gateway connect timeout for streaming endpoints and limit retries for streaming to avoid cascading duplicate streams; plan in next sprint.
Jess (support): Customers asked for summary and SLA credit timeline. I'll draft initial customer-facing note.
CarrierBot: Provider final note at 10:02 UTC — memory leak in transit device causing session resets; patch deployed. Route stability restored at ~09:35 UTC.
Tom (sre-oncall): Marking incident as mitigated at 09:42 UTC, will keep incident channel open until postmortem. Creating PagerDuty follow-up to schedule RCA.
Lina (support-ops): Postmortem tasks: capture gateway logs, collect pcap from provider, billing reconciliation, update runbook for apse2 fallback. I'll create tasks in the incident tracker.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Thanks — will add trace IDs and logs to the postmortem doc.
Jess (support): Closing customer notifications, will send consolidated update once the RCA is in. :thumbsup:
Tom (sre-oncall): Thanks team — good triage and quick fallback.
